claims.statement: `ExecutorKind` enumerates every runtime the server can name — 'mock', 'opencode', 'codex', 'claude', 'hermes', 'gemini', 'editor', 'pi', 'docker', 'deep-agent', and 'custom' — and the ExecutionEngine constructor always registers the eight defaults mock/opencode/codex/claude/hermes/gemini/editor/pi while registering deep-agent only when DJIMIT_DEEP_ENABLED=true (also instantiating the DeepAgentContractIssuer).

`docker` and `custom` are never registered by the constructor: 'docker' only appears as the kind reported by DockerSandboxExecutor when the engine wraps another executor at dispatch time, and 'custom' is the extension slot for out-of-tree implementations added via registerExecutor().

The TaskExecutor contract is `kind`, `start(task, options) → Promise<ExecutionSession>`, `canExecute(task) → boolean`, and optional `buildCommand(task, options) → { command, args }`; buildCommand is what lets DockerSandboxExecutor re-host an inner executor's CLI invocation without re-implementing argument construction.

ExecutionSession exposes `events: AsyncIterable<ExecutionEventCreateInput>` (persisted + broadcast by processEventStream), `result: Promise<ExecutionResult>`, `closed?: Promise<void>` (resolves only after the OS child and its streams close), mandatory `cancel()`, and optional, currently-unimplemented `pause()`/`resume()`.

ExecutionFailure carries `retryable` and `sideEffectsPossible`; the engine's normalizeFailure forces retryable=false whenever sideEffectsPossible is true, and nextRetryExecutor refuses any retry if attempt >= maxRetries, !failure.retryable, or failure.sideEffectsPossible — so post-side-effect failures never chain-hop providers.

All CLI adapters share runtime plumbing: runtime-process.ts (runtimeProcessClosed + SIGTERM→SIGKILL-after-5s stopRuntimeProcess that resolves on actual close), executor-env.ts (buildExecutorEnv allowlists safe env so server secrets stay out of spawned CLIs), captureExecutorOutput (5 MiB rolling stdout/stderr tail), and structured-runtime-event.ts (maps tool_use/tool_result/error/text JSON chunks from claude/gemini/editor/codex/opencode/pi into TOOL_CALL/TOOL_RESULT/ERROR/LOG events with usage).

The skip-permissions boundary is operator-armed: resolveExecutorSkipPermissions returns true only when task metadata requested it AND RUNTIME_ALLOW_SKIP_PERMISSIONS==='true', and ExecutionEngine.startExecutionAttempt only forwards skipPermissions to the adapter when that guard passes (a test asserts all four combinations). Per-executor * _SKIP_PERMISSIONS envs remain a second default layer.

DockerSandboxExecutor wraps an inner TaskExecutor, requires inner.buildCommand (else DOCKER_SANDBOX_INNER_COMMAND_UNAVAILABLE), reports kind:'docker', and enforces non-root user (1000:1000), --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read-only root + tmpfs /tmp (64 MiB), networkMode 'none' by default, cpu 1.0 / memory 512m, --rm cleanup, and a digest-pinned image (DOCKER_SANDBOX_IMAGE must contain @sha256:; DOCKER_SANDBOX_SKIP_DIGEST_CHECK=true bypasses with a warning and is NOT recommended for production). These invariants are asserted in docker-sandbox-executor.test.ts.

The engine creates a DockerSandboxExecutor inside startExecutionAttempt when task.metadata.sandbox.enabled===true, overriding image/cpu/memory/network/bind-mounts on DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG; deep-agent is explicitly forbidden from this Docker sandboxing path ('Deep Agent sandboxing is controlled by the sovereign runtime').

DeepAgentExecutor is gated on a signed contract: canExecute requires task.metadata.deep_agent_contract with identity.task_id matching this task and capabilities.profile_id==='no-tool-canary'; start() throws DEEP_AGENT_CONTRACT_INVALID_FOR_TASK otherwise. The remote transport accepts only an HTTP loopback or literal Tailscale IPv4 DJIMIT_DEEP_URL and fails closed on non-zero exit, timeout, oversized response, or unparseable final status.

deep-agent never participates in fallback: when its circuit breaker is open the engine throws instead of falling back, and nextRetryExecutor returns null for a failed deep-agent attempt — a contract-gated run is terminal by design.

CircuitBreakerService keeps per-ExecutorKind state CLOSED→OPEN→HALF_OPEN→CLOSED: CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD consecutive failures (default 3) in a 60s sliding window opens the circuit, canExecute returns false while OPEN until CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOVERY_MS (default 30s), then one probe is allowed in HALF_OPEN and 2 consecutive successes close it again.

FallbackChainService maps each ExecutionMode to an ordered provider list (fast: opencode→gemini→claude; standard: claude→codex→gemini; controlled: claude→codex; restricted: claude only) and getNextAvailable walks the chain after the current kind, skipping breakers that are open; custom chains can be injected via constructor or setChain().

maxRetries per attempt comes from ExecutionModePolicyService by mode (fast:1, standard:2, controlled:3, restricted:0), so even a retryable failure cannot chain-hop in restricted mode; fallbacks are re-admitted through the policy gate (fallbackAdmitted) and each hop is persisted with failureCode, failureDomain, retryable, and sideEffectsPossible.

The production Dockerfile pins @openai/codex@0.146.0, opencode-ai@1.18.10, and @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.282 globally and build-time-verifies them with git/codex/opencode/claude --version probes; the same layer installs the gh CLI as a static .deb pinned via ARG GH_CLI_VERSION=2.100.0 (verified with gh --version) for GithubPrReviewService, which shells out to gh for PR review comments and Check Runs. At runtime GET /swarms/runtime-readiness treats only codex and opencode as production runtimes, checks their binary contracts and provider credentials, returns ready/blocked_reasons per runtime, and never starts a worker (starts_workers: false).

Before spawning a loop worker, LoopWorkerExecutorService probes the lease runtime via LoopService.getRuntimeContract(), records a start worker manifest with the contract, and if the contract is unavailable or status is not ok records a fail manifest with blocked_reasons runtime_contract_drift, fails the lease with runtime_contract_unavailable_or_drifted, and throws RUNTIME_CONTRACT_DRIFTED — no provider process is spawned against a drifted contract.

RuntimeCommandService.getRuntimeContract probes each CLI runtime with <bin> --version plus a --help probe, marks the contract drifted when required json/cwd/headless flags are missing from the help output, stamps a sha256 conformance contract_hash with named checks (runtime_available, contract_not_drifted, structured_events, usage_accounting, bounded_lifecycle), caches contracts for LOOP_RUNTIME_CONTRACT_CACHE_MS (default 5s), and persists probes to the runtime_contract_probes table.

The LoopService runtime contract set covers manual, mock, codex, opencode, claude, gemini, editor, and pi, exposed via getRuntimeContracts() at GET /loops/runtime-contracts; the manual runtime is always available (status ok, proof_class static) but LoopWorkerExecutorService.executeMaker rejects manual maker leases with MANUAL_MAKER_REQUIRES_HUMAN, and manual checkers require an explicit non-manual runtime to dispatch (CHECKER_RUNTIME_REQUIRED).

OpenCodeExecutor reports token usage and cost collected from NDJSON step_finish parts as tokenUsage (running max of part.tokens.total) and costDollars (running max of part.cost) metrics on the ExecutionResult; it also accumulates the step totals into a separate tokenSum used to enforce the OPENCODE_MAX_RUN_TOKENS runaway brake, and resolves an exit-0 run as failed with code VERIFICATION_FAILED (retryable: false, sideEffectsPossible: true, failureDomain: 'opencode') when a deduplicated verification tool step failure was detected.
CodexExecutor sums usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens from turn.completed NDJSON events into the result tokenUsage metric.

OpenCodeExecutor.getVerificationFailure treats a tool_use event as a verification step when the tool is named build_check/lint/test/typecheck/type-check or is a bash tool whose state.input.command matches type-?check/tsc/eslint/vitest/jest/pytest/cargo test/go test/npm (run )?test, and reports failure when state.status is error/failed/rejected/cancelled or state.output parses as JSON with success === false, a non-zero numeric exitCode, verdict === 'fail', or summary.failed_count > 0 (non-JSON output is ignored).

OpenCodeExecutor.parseJsonEvent accepts any line that parses to a JSON object with a string type and returns null otherwise; collectMetricsFromText buffers partial lines across chunks so only newline-terminated input is evaluated (remainder flushed on close), and metrics are fed from both stdout and stderr, while payload reads fall back from the nested part envelope to the flattened event for version-drifted output.

OpenCode step token accounting is tested at two levels: opencode-token-brake.test.ts proves the OPENCODE_MAX_RUN_TOKENS brake stops a run whose summed step tokens pass the cap well before the wall-clock timeout, and opencode-token-usage.test.ts pins LoopService.extractRuntimeUsage summing opencode step_finish token fields into prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens (usage_source 'runtime_stdout') — the regression fix for loop-reported tokens_used always being 0.

Adapter registration in the ExecutionEngine constructor does not establish production readiness: the README lists 8 default adapters (OpenCode, Codex, Claude, Hermes, Gemini, Pi, Editor, Mock) with Deep Agents opt-in, while the /swarms/runtime-readiness gate treats only codex and opencode as production runtimes and blocks anything else with non_mock_supported_runtime_required.
